units.translation: On this verse nothing is noted in the Medicean scholia; recent interpreters understand ἐστί [is] with κόναβος [the din], which although everyone knows is very often omitted, nevertheless whoever compares the preceding similar verses, each of which has some more significant verb added, will judge it hardly likely that no weightier verb was at hand for Aeschylus here than that weak ἐστί [is], and that not even expressed, but to be supplied in thought. But here too Aeschylus has been made unlike himself not by his own fault but by that of the scribes. Hence I conjectured κόναβος ἐν πύλαις δεινὰ προμυχθίζει χαλκοδέτων σακέων [the din of bronze-bound shields groans terribly in the gates], with a dochmiac trimeter placed among dimeters, just as in the first part of this song trimeters and dimeters are mixed. After ἐν πύλαις [in the gates] two syllables have fallen out, which although they can easily be supplied so that ἐν πύλαισι δὲ [and in the gates] is written, nevertheless it is more probable that some disyllabic word has fallen out, such as δεινά [terribly], which I inserted by way of example. The verb προμυχθίζει [groans forth] I supplied from a gloss of Hesychius written thus in the codex, προμυχθίζει χαλκοδεσμῶν ὁπλῶν: ἀντὶ τοῦ προσχωρίου [groans forth of bronze-bound weapons: instead of advances]. Which are to be arranged thus, προμυχθίζει χαλκοδέτων σακέων: ἀντὶ τοῦ πρόσω χωρεῖ χαλκοδέσμων ὅπλων [groans forth of bronze-bound shields: instead of advances of bronze-bound weapons]. More briefly Photius p. 455, 25 προμυθίζει: πρόσω χωρεῖ [advances], where προμυθίζει [advances] is written for προμυχθίζει [groans forth] either by a scribal error or by Photius himself, since the gloss is placed before προμυλαία [the forecourt], although not much weight should be given to this argument, since the order is often neglected by Photius. Aeschylus used another compound of this verb, ἀναμυχθίζεσθαι [to groan back], in Prometheus v. 743.
